observations.statement: Both pages find the target paragraph exactly once, at the same position and with the same computed styles (color rgb(85,85,85), opacity 1, visible, display block, no ancestors with a non-default opacity, filter or blend). Computed style and layout of the paragraph itself do not differ between the pages.
In transfer-a, the text rectangle contains no text-coloured pixels. Every sampled pixel has the single value 239, at both viewports.
In transfer-b, the same rectangle contains dark glyph pixels down to the text colour value 85, on a mostly white (255) background, at both viewports.

In transfer-a, the top hit-test element at all 15 text points is section#delivery (position relative, z-index auto, opaque white background). The paragraph comes second (targetIndex 1). In transfer-b, the paragraph is the top element at all 15 text points (targetIndex 0).
In transfer-a, the reported border box of section#delivery begins at y=345, below every point where it is hit, including text points at y=310–317 and the reference point at y=338.

The paragraph lies inside section#summary, whose background is opaque white and whose box spans y 135–345. In transfer-b, white (255) dominates both the text clip and the reference clip, as that background would predict. In transfer-a, the same region reads 239.
The body and html backgrounds are rgb(238,240,236), which fits a grey value of about 239.
The layouts differ: main is 632px tall in transfer-a and 648px in transfer-b, and section#delivery does not appear in transfer-b's reference stack at y=338.

explanations.claim: transfer-a shows the reported defect, at both viewports. The price note is laid out and styled to be visible, but nothing of it reaches the screen; transfer-b renders the same text normally.

In transfer-a, an opaque layer hides the text. The layer belongs to section#delivery for hit-testing and sits above the paragraph. Because delivery is position:relative and comes later in the DOM, it paints over the static content of #summary.

The covering layer extends above #delivery's own border box (hit at y 304–344 while the box starts at 345), and its colour (~239) matches the page background rather than delivery's white background. Together this suggests a generated box, such as a ::before or ::after pseudo-element with the page background colour and a negative offset. Hit-testing attributes such a box to its originating element, and it would not change delivery's rect.

The cover's lower edge appears to lie just above y=345. In transfer-a's reference clip (y 328–347), 17 rows read 239, 1 row reads 218 (probably delivery's top border at y=345) and 2 rows read 255 (delivery's white background). In transfer-b, the same clip shows summary white with a border row and a 3-row page-background gap.

contradictions.description: The hit-test reports #delivery at points outside its own reported border box. A plain box background cannot do this, and neither can a transform or negative margin, since both would move the reported rect. The pseudo-element explanation is an inference made to fit this mismatch; it was not observed.

#delivery's computed background is white (255), but the covered area reads 239. So delivery's own background cannot be what is painted there, which weakens any reading of this as delivery's box simply overlapping. Something that hit-tests as delivery but paints in the page background colour has to be assumed.
The paragraph's own computed styles are identical on both pages. Explanations based on the paragraph's colour, opacity, visibility or ancestor effects are therefore ruled out.

main is 16px taller in transfer-b, and delivery is absent from transfer-b's reference stack. So the two pages also differ in layout, not only in an overlay, and the difference between the pages may involve more than one change.

uncertainties.question: What exactly paints over the text in transfer-a: a pseudo-element of #delivery, or something else such as a box-shadow combined with a hit-test-extending mechanism?
uncertainties.whyNotResolvable: The broker cannot observe pseudo-elements, CSS source, paint order or compositing layers. elementsFromPoint only names originating elements.
uncertainties.nextMeasurement: Have the broker run getComputedStyle(#delivery, '::before') and getComputedStyle(#delivery, '::after') (content, position, top, height, background-color, z-index), or temporarily set #delivery {visibility:hidden} and resample the text clip.

uncertainties.question: Does 239 in the pixel statistics really correspond to rgb(238,240,236)?
uncertainties.whyNotResolvable: The probe code does not document how the broker converts RGB to the single channel used in its statistics.
uncertainties.nextMeasurement: Sample per-channel RGB at one text point in transfer-a, for example (720,314).

uncertainties.question: Where does #delivery sit in transfer-b, and why is main 16px taller there?
uncertainties.whyNotResolvable: The probe only records stacks at points near the paragraph. #delivery did not appear in any transfer-b stack, so its rect was never captured.
uncertainties.nextMeasurement: Query the rect and computed margin-top of #delivery on both pages.

uncertainties.question: Is the text covered in other states, such as after scrolling or at other viewports?
uncertainties.whyNotResolvable: Only scrollY=0 at two viewports was measured.
uncertainties.nextMeasurement: Repeat the text-clip pixel sample at other scroll offsets and widths.
